# Testing

Runner: `node --test` (bare - a trailing `test/` path breaks discovery on
Node 22). Suite: 0 tests across 0 files.

**THE ARENA2-GATED PINS ARE HALF-BLIND, AND THAT IS A KNOWN COST.** A
pin behind `{ skip: skipReal }` never runs on CI, so a law change that
contradicts it goes unnoticed until someone runs the suite WITH game
data. Two did (2026-08-23, found while merging the input arc):
audit18_hosts_dungeon's swing-fatigue pin still asserted the drain
AUDIT 24 wave 42 had deliberately moved to the hosts, and
cityguards.test.js's stub renderer lacked the `destroyBillboardBatch`
wave 6's batch-free calls - it THREW rather than failed. Both are
fixed, and both by making the pin say MORE, not less. When you change
a law, grep the ARENA2-gated files for it too.

**AND THEY ARE ENGLISH-RETAIL-LOCKED, WHICH NOTHING SAID.** 2026-08-25:
the gated pins ran in a working environment for the first time, against
a real ARENA2 pulled from the DaggerfallSetup installer. 35 of them
failed, and NONE of the 35 is a port defect. 8 fail on FILENAME CASE
alone - retail data was written on a filesystem that did not care, and
that install carries `INVE00I0.img` beside `INVE04I0.IMG` and
`ANIM0001.vid` beside `ANIM0002.VID`, 76 lowercase names among 1,598.
The shipping data path already knew (`dataSource.normalizeName`
uppercases on both ingest and lookup, so the browser is fine); the test
harness and the vite dev middleware read the folder case-sensitively,
so `npm run dev` 404'd against files that were sitting right there.
The dev server is case-insensitive now; the pins still read the folder
literally and a mixed-case corpus still reddens them.

The other 27 are LOCALISATION. That install is the German edition, and
these pins encode the English retail corpus by value: FACTION.TXT has
374 records against the pinned 366 and names faction 41 Kriegergilde,
the map directory has no location called "Privateer's Hold" so five
dungeon pins dereference null, SPELLS.STD's indices move, CLASS*.CFG
carries different career flags (a Mage there CAN wear plate), and the
IMG corpus is 198 files against 263. Every one of those is the data
being legitimately different, not the port being wrong.

Two port-relevant facts fell out of the same run and are recorded
rather than fixed, because both change shipped behaviour: the
CLASS*.CFG NAME FIELD IS ENCIPHERED in that edition (CLASS00 reads
"vfu", CLASS15 reads "dfhdfh" - a repeated three-gram where German's
Barbar is a repeated three-gram, so the record parses correctly and
only the name is coded) and `chargenSession` falls back to
CLASS_CAREERS only when the name is EMPTY, so a non-English install
shows gibberish in the class list; and the port's font maps the
high-bit range to punctuation, so every umlaut renders as `#` or `}`
("St#rke", "W}ste"). Neither can be caught by any pin the suite has,
because the suite has never had non-English data.

All four hosts route both look sites (mouse and touch) through the filter - no raw delta reaches the camera - and tick it on the frame's unscaled dt before the camera is read; the screen's range is DFU's clamp (0..0.9), not the 'ours' 0..1 it had. Campaign: 5 mutants (the fraction formula, no SmoothingMax clamp, target unclamped, the wrong fraction kept, a host never ticks), 5 killed. Rule: a probe that presses keys at a host which mounts the wizard must carry a headless-chargen skip. The ALLOWLIST for the probes that drive the wizard on purpose is self-checking on both sides - a member that grows a `class=` skip has stopped being a chargen probe, and a member that never reads `__chargenFlow` was only ever parked there to silence the rule; either fails. The third pin is `tradeModeProbe`'s second lie: 500,000 gold is 1250 kg at `goldPieceWeightInKg`, against a MaxEncumbrance near 90, so every sale it made correctly took ConfirmTrade's letter-of-credit branch while the probe asserted coins - it walks BOTH arms deliberately now and reads the window's own weighing rather than recomputing it. T3 ADDS THREE MORE, on the same disease one step further along: a probe whose EXIT CODE has nothing to do with whether its subject worked. T2 caught `guildServiceProbe` printing OK and exiting 0 on a run where its character had been turned away at the Mages Guild door and no service ran at all. Rule: every browser probe must judge something, and must not print three or more states AFTER its last judgement - that second clause is what catches the guildService shape, whose three exits were all setup guards with ten unjudged prints behind them. EYEBALL TOOLS are exempt (screenshot.mjs, musicRender.mjs and four others whose output is a PNG or a WAV for a human), and that allowlist is self-checking too: a member must actually write a file. THE SURVEY THAT FOUND THE SIX WAS WRONG THREE TIMES FIRST, always accusing working code by missing an idiom - the local `die()`/`fail()` helpers, then the `check()` harness, then the accumulate-and-exit shape `process.exit(ok ? 0 : 1)` that castProbe and firstHourProbe use between them for 45 judgements. The vocabulary is written down in the file so the next sweep does not re-derive it wrong. ROAD-E E8 added three, one per probe of Port-Ledger.md:580: the retired `shopProbe.mjs` name must stay absent while `tradeModeProbe`/`nativeTradeProbe` carry its subject; `toneProbe.mjs` may not hunt the `tone: Normal` TEXT row the native talk window draws as art, and must read `native` and `topicMode` instead; and `worldWhereIsProbe.mjs`'s boot-box drain must sit BEFORE its walker poll and judge itself - a modal holds the motor, so a probe that polls first polls a frozen world. |

The fix is EF1c's own rule, strip quoted spans then look; the quote is verbatim again and the asserted count is gone, because nothing measured it. THE STRIP MUST BE WHOLE-FILE AND THEN BOUNDED: comments wrap, and the quotation that forced the workaround wraps (opening quote and token on one line, close on the next), so a per-line strip sees an unpaired quote and strips nothing - but prose quotes do not always pair, so a generous span mis-pairs and blanks whatever sits between two unrelated quotes, and a 400-character bound did exactly that on the first run and swallowed talkMacros' GetValue flag, an OPEN one. Two newlines reaches a wrapped quotation and cannot reach across a paragraph. THE FAILURE DIRECTION IS THE DESIGN: missing a quotation leaves a retired flag listed, which a reader can see and dismiss; blanking an open flag hides real work, which nobody sees at all. The rule now lives in tools/flagSites.mjs and the tool and the AUDIT 18 guard both IMPORT it - they had a copy each, and the guard went red the moment the tool learned the new rule, which is exactly what two copies buys. 165 sites -> 155. What IN1 REFUSED: the past-tense case (a block naming a flag to say it is gone) is prose - a heuristic over it flagged guildServiceWindow's "FLAGGED: DFU binds each button to a DaggerfallShortcut hotkey" and a dozen like it, open flags whose blocks merely carry history. | overlayreentry.test.js | 7 | THE CRASH OF 2026-08-29 - "InternalError: too much recursion", fifty frames of closeOverlay -> onClose -> _close -> dispose -> closeOverlay, off the LIVE SITE. Every close path of the rest window reached it in the two exterior hosts. TWO HALVES, PINNED APART, because either alone stops the crash and leaving the other broken leaves the next window to find it. THE HOST'S ORDER: every drain in townTalk disposed the occupant and cleared the slot AFTER, and dispose() runs host code - S40 opened that door on purpose so a window can vacate the slot before handing control on (DFU's PopToHUD runs before RaiseSkills and the level-up screen needs it free), so the re-entrant close read a slot still pointing at the window being disposed and disposed it again, for ever. THE WINDOW'S DISPATCH: RestWindow._close is deliberately unguarded on `done` - clearing a boolean twice is clearing it once - but it also fires onClose, and firing THAT twice is a second PopToHUD. These are BEHAVIOUR pins and not source sweeps: the slot is closure state and the window is a plain class, so the whole loop reproduces in Node with no GL and no ARENA2, and createTownTalk builds without either (nothing loads until ensureLoaded) - so the REAL host is driven, not a stand-in. Six doors are enumerated from restWindow.js's own _close call sites (the ended page on a key and on a click, the refusal page, backing out of the selection page, the host closing the slot, the host disposing the window) and each must leave the window done, the slot empty, and onClose owed EXACTLY ONCE - the fix must not buy safety by dropping the callback, since that resurrects the AUDIT 21 F3 defect where advancement.js dumps every point into the LOWEST stats. Then each half is pinned against the other being broken: the window survives a host that still disposes before clearing (the shape every drain had the day before), and the host survives a window with no dispatch guard at all (which is every other window in the tree). Plus the real host's own drains - closeOverlay, the key drain, and showOverlay replacing an occupant, which now holds the SUCCESSOR before the outgoing window is told, so an outgoing window that closes this slot finds the new occupant and its identity guard leaves it alone. And a source sweep on top, because the behaviour pins can only reach the drains a headless test can drive: nothing in townTalk.js may dispose the overlay slot outside the one drain, and the drain is read IN ORDER - the slot emptied before the window is disposed, which is the fix itself. Campaign: 8 mutants, 8 killed, and the eighth needed a code change to earn its death - closeOverlay's own `!overlay` check made dropOverlay's unreachable, and a guard no mutation can kill is a guard no reader can trust, so the door keeps the identity check and the drain owns the empty-slot one. |

THE TWO MODE CYCLES DISAGREE, and it is DFU's own: PlayerActivate.NextInteractionMode walks the enum (Steal > Grab > Info > Talk) and the panel walks Steal > TALK > GRAB > Info, so clicking the bar's mode button and pressing the mode key move through the same four modes in different orders - reusing the keyboard's cycle passes any "it cycles" pin and dies here. The right click is the exact inverse of the panel's own, round-tripped from every mode. DOCKED collapses AutoSizeModes.ScaleToFit's arithmetic to the screen's full width in proportion, flush to the bottom (an integer-floored scale leaves a gap and fails); UNDOCKED is the native scale times LargeHUDUndockedScale with alignment None FORCED to Centre, so 0 and 2 are the same bar. The compass frame is a C# `(int)` TRUNCATION over 32 frames, walked at 401 headings to prove nothing indexes past the last, with the port's wrap covering the 1.0 DFU's own read can never produce. Only the MAP panel differs on the right button (the automap left, the travel map right); every other panel binds ONE handler to both, which is checked from the other side. And every panel posts an ACTION ui/input.js routes - the same door the keyboard uses, driven through a recording ctx - with the five arms U45 added reporting honestly when no host has grown a door and the four that predate it returning true regardless, pinned as the inconsistency it is. Plus the four-hosts wiring: all four DRAW the bar, and the four that own a pointer offer it the click and bind ActivateCursor. 11 mutations, 11 killed + D10 shipped the two OFFSETS this subject used to record as read by nothing: horseOffsetHeight is the drawn bar's height and NEVER asks about docking (TransportManager.cs:304-309, the (int) truncation included), weaponOffsetHeight is FORCED whenever the bar is docked whatever the setting says (FPSWeapon.cs:146-155) and consults the setting only undocked, both answer 0 on a null HUD, and the offset really moves the horse rect (moved, not resized) and the viewmodel quad. That is the corpus gate, and all three shipping files pass it to the byte. ALL THREE CARRY 32 FRAMES and differ in SIZE - 48x40, 34x28, 30x25 - so a reader that hardcoded the standard needle's dimensions would decode two of the three as garbage while consuming exactly the right number of bytes; both come from the header. It taught that a truncated body was a load failure leaving no record behind; ReadImageData (BssFile.cs:210-222) does no such thing - BinaryReader.ReadBytes returns a SHORT array at end of stream instead of throwing, and `new DFBitmap[0]` is legal, so Read() never enters its catch and Load returns TRUE for a truncated body and for a zero-frame header alike. ONLY A NEGATIVE header count or frame size throws (`new byte[-1]`). Two tiers per module:
1. **Synthetic fixtures** - in-memory data built inside the test. Always run;
   CI stays green with no game data (88 pass, 49 skip).
2. **Real-data validation** - gated on `ARENA2_PATH`; skip cleanly when
   absent. Pin observed counts, names, ids, checksums, and structural
   closure invariants.

Without game data the suite runs 805 pass / 120 skip (AUDIT 18 corrected
the long-stale "88 pass, 49 skip", which described a 137-test suite that
has not existed for many milestones). Those 75 skipped pins DO NOT RUN
IN THE DEPLOY GATE - CI has no ARENA2 - so a real-data pin is a local
gate only. (Measured on main at the AUDIT 18 merge; recount by hand
when the split moves.) `manifest.test.js` guards the totals above but not this line;
recount it by hand when the split moves.

Sourcing data in a fresh session: `sh tools/fetch-data.sh`, then
`ARENA2_PATH=/home/claude/dfdata/arena2 npm test`.

Visual proof: `npm run shot [out.png]` boots vite in-process and drives the
provisioned Chromium (playwright@1.56.0 <-> /opt/pw-browsers chromium-1194;
bump both together). CONTRACT: the scene query rides the SHOT_QUERY env
var, NOT argv (`SHOT_QUERY='shot&world&tod=22:00' npm run shot out.png`) -
argv[2] is only the output path. SHOT_TIMEOUT overrides the 30s ready
wait (streaming world wants 90000); SHOT_EVAL runs a JS snippet in-page
after ready (promise-returning expressions are awaited - top-level
`await` fails). Shot-mode probe hooks in the dungeon and world scenes:
window.__move(dx, dy, dz), window.__pose(x, y, z, yaw, pitch),
window.__player {pos, warp}, and in the dungeon __activate/__activateKey/
__ray/__actions. SwiftShader renders heavy scenes at ~7 fps headless -
time-based proofs must poll state, never trust wall-clock. `?shot` in main.js fixes the vantage and raises
`window.__shotReady`. Manual proof, not a suite gate.

Playing the game: `ARENA2_PATH=... npm run firsthour` drives ONE character
through one continuous session on the real hosts - chargen, the starting
dungeon, a fight, the loot, the way out, the road, a town, a shop, a
purchase, a bed - asserting the player is alive and the state coherent at
each step, with a screenshot per stage (`SHOTS=<dir>`, default
`firsthour-shots/`). A failing stage does NOT stop the walk; its dependents
are marked skipped and the run continues, because the output is a MAP of
what a first hour hits rather than the first pothole. `ONLY_CHARGEN=1` stops
after the wizard - a four-minute run instead of twenty-five, which is how
the modal-ownership fix was red-proofed. It is a TOOL, not a suite gate: it
needs game data and about twenty-five minutes of SwiftShader. Run it when a
host, a window or the boot path changes - `tools/nativeTradeProbe.mjs` sat
red for months because nothing did.

PX31 (2026-08-31) found the same rot ACROSS THE FLEET, and one line up
from any assertion: NINE probes waited on `#enhanced-menu .railbtn` at
their front door. `railbtn` is the SHELL rail's class and the boot door
has not carried one since PX1 replaced it with the pixel home, whose
buttons were classless - so every one of them timed out before its
first check, and had since 2026-08-27. The fix is a hook rather than
nine text selectors: the door's buttons carry `doorbtn door-<id>` and
the probes select on that, because matching on the visible words would
be the same bug waiting on a relabel. Opening the door then showed the
rot goes deeper in at least two of them - `enhancedPackProbe` and
`enhancedDollProbe` still assert the U53 slot map (`.node`,
`.node.filled`) that PX19d and PX20a replaced with the worn map. Those
bodies are a repair of their own and are NOT done, which is why PX31's
own pin is a new file (`tools/enhancedPackLayoutProbe.mjs`) rather than
more checks bolted to a probe that cannot reach them.

THE STANDING LESSON IS SHARPER THAN "RUN THE PROBES": a probe that
cannot reach its first check fails identically to a probe nobody ran,
and neither shows up anywhere. A red probe is evidence; an unreachable
one is silence wearing evidence's clothes.

Pre-push gate: `npm run check` (test + build).

Drift guard: `test/manifest.test.js` pins the total line and every row of
the table above against the real suite. Recalculate this doc in the same
commit as any test change.
| stalechunk.test.js | 4 | THE BUILD MOVED WHILE THE PAGE WAS OPEN. A player reported `boot failed: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module` on the deployed site, and the build was SOUND - a fresh one fetches every chunk, so no test that loads ONE build can see this. It lives between two of them: index.html hard-references SEVENTEEN hashed chunk URLs, every deploy renames EIGHT of them (main and the four enhanced screens among them, because scripts/buildTag.mjs stamps the sha into a module main imports and the change cascades), GitHub Pages DELETES the old artifact rather than keeping it beside the new one, and main is redeployed several times a day. A returning player's cached index is a map of a build that is gone, and the LAZY chunks are the exposed ones because a first visit never fetched them. THE RECOVERY IS A RELOAD, and what is pinned here is the ladder that decides on one. TWO WAYS IT GOES WRONG, both held: not hearing a browser - Chrome, Firefox, Safari and Vite's CSS preloader say this four different ways, and a check that knew only Chrome's would leave the other three on the dead page, so the LIST is what answers rather than a regex written twice; and reloading TWICE, which is an infinite loop pointed at a player who has no error to report and nothing to press, so the second failure gets words instead. The words are pinned to be about the PLAYER rather than about a module graph. A boot that WORKS gives the reload back, or the flag outlives the problem and the next deploy finds the retry spent; every sessionStorage touch is shielded because it THROWS outright in some privacy modes, and no memory means no free reload - the safe way to be wrong. Live proof is tools/staleChunkProbe.mjs, which builds the site TWICE and hands the browser the older index on its first document: 10/10, and its CONTROL run rebuilds with the recovery removed and reproduces the reported sentence verbatim. That control failed its own first run with an empty body - the control build's eager chunks were not cached either, so the page never booted and the check passed for the wrong reason. |

THE SOURCE LIST: updateNpcBase adds `base` (mXbaseanim1st) and then, only if different, the corrected actor skeleton - and addSingleAnimSource DROPS a source the archive lacks rather than refusing. play() then searches mAnimSources IN REVERSE ("last-inserted source has priority") and takes the first whose text keys give the group a valid range - the WHOLE of reset() must succeed, so a source carrying a start key and no stop key is passed OVER rather than refused, while hasAnimation is a different question answered by ANY source. The fixture arrangement is the pin: a female actor with the x-form .kf really has two sources, armidle.kf and armfpweapon.kf name different groups, and the idle is won by one file while the equip and the swing are won by the other - so "which source won" is measured by RE-POSING the assembly with each file's tracks and requiring the live arm to match the one it named. AND RULE 56 WAS WRONG IN A SHIPPED MODULE, found by the mutation campaign rather than by reading: the accum root was ported as "the topmost tracked bone" where the reference is a TWO-NAME TABLE, `{ "bip01", "root bone" }`, bip01 preferred, and a candidate accepted only when the KF DRIVES it. On a first-person weapon .kf - which keys nothing on bip01 - the old rule answered an UPPER ARM, and any translation channel on that bone would then have had its X and Y pinned to rest, deforming the arm instead of moving the actor. It is also STICKY: `if (!mAccumRoot)` means the FIRST source to resolve one wins for the life of the rig, so the pin runs the fixtures BOTH ways round - because the arrangement where the only source with an accum root is already the last cannot tell "first non-null" from "last source" apart. The old pin asserted the defect in as many words ("the accumulation root is the topmost tracked bone") and is replaced; the flight-extraction pin keeps its fixture and now passes its accum root explicitly, because the CHOICE and the EXTRACTION are two rules and only one of them needs Morrowind's vocabulary. 19 mutants, 19 dead. |

A mesh tinted twice looks like a dark mesh; a weapon at its bone's bare origin looks like a weapon. RULE 63, whose own opening line is "the single most likely place for a port to be silently wrong", and the port was doing the wrong one: the packer wrote the raw vertex colour and the shader MULTIPLIED it into the albedo, where OpenMW SUBSTITUTES the whole vec4 for whichever material channel the colour MODE names. The mode - not the presence of a colour array - is the guard, so the pin runs the same colours through two modes and requires two different packed streams. RULES 64 + 66, the mode itself, which the port had no notion of: a colour array ALONE selects AmbientAndDiffuse; NiVertexColorProperty overrides it; and `lightmode` is assigned ONLY inside the SrcAmbDif branch, so an ancestor property still blacks the surface out after a NEARER one has taken the mode. That one rule is why the property chain became an ordered root-first LIST instead of a map keyed by type - a map cannot produce the pair, and matprops.nif's "Scoped" shape is authored to demand it. Also pinned from those rules: a colour mode on a COLOURLESS mesh is undone to WHITE and never black; a material on an ANCESTOR NiNode reaches the shape (the common Morrowind authoring pattern); and Morrowind specular is parsed and thrown away, so glossiness is a constant zero rather than the file's 42. RULE 65: only DrawMode 3 (Both) is two-sided and "Default" is a synonym for counter-clockwise WITH culling. RULE 14, `BoneOffset`, absent from the reverted arc and from this port until now - the match is ciEqual and EXACT, the scan is pre-order and stops at the first hit, and DRAWABLES are skipped (`apply(osg::Geometry&)` is an empty override), so boneoffset.nif carries a decoy SHAPE named "boneoffset" earlier in pre-order, the real marker named "BoneOFFSET" (which == against the literal does not match), and a third node after it; three separate mistakes yield three different answers. It rides the same PositionAttitudeTransform as rule 13's mirror and a PAT is T * R * S, so the offset is applied AFTER the negation - the pin asserts -2 + 3 = 1 and not -(2 + 3), and a live pin poses the real weapon twice and requires it to move by the offset's own LENGTH, because a `boneOffset` field the placement never reads draws exactly what MW-D12 drew. RULES 58 + 59, the names the loader refuses to draw: "Bounding Box" takes its whole SUBTREE out of the scene EXCEPT when it is the root (mRootNode is null on the first call - it reads like an oversight and is load-bearing), and the geometry skip list is not one rule but two, with "shadow" and "tri shadow" UNCONDITIONAL where "tri editormarker" is gated on the ROOT carrying "MRK" compared with == rather than ciEqual. Two fixture files differing ONLY in that flag are what tells a gated skip from an unconditional one; the MRK-less one carries two decoys (a lower-case "mrk" on the root, a correct "MRK" on a NON-root node) so both wrong readings fail. RULE 30's other half: the neck factor is `0.75 + 0.25 * mAimingFactor`, not the constant the port shipped - it snaps to 1 while `mUpperBodyState > WeaponEquipped` and ramps down at 0.5 a SECOND, pinned frame-rate independent (two half-steps equal one whole step) and through the live arm, which raises its aim on a swing in one 16ms frame and lets it fall afterwards. MW-D12's machine is what made rule 30 reachable at all: with a constant idle there was no aiming state to be in, which is why the constant was honest when it was written and a gap now. 35 mutants, 35 dead. |

Without that gate a bare-handed player whose .kf has no idlehh idles in idle1h, the one-handed SWORD stance, fist raised as if holding a blade; and a missing handtohand becomes weapononehand, so empty hands MIME a sword swing. ## PY1 - THE PARITY PINS WERE BLIND (2026-08-28)

**Fourteen pins across eight files were reporting green by never
running.** They are not remembered-value pins - they REGENERATE a port
table from Daggerfall Unity's own C# and compare it cell for cell:
ENEMY_BASICS off `EnemyBasics.cs`, LOOT_MATRICES off `LootTables.cs`,
the ingredient ITEM_GROUPS and artifact rows off `ItemEnums.cs`,
MAGIC_ONLY_KEYS off the effect classes, the race templates,
PlayerActivate's ladder, the two enemy-motor waves,
`DaggerfallInterior`, and MacroHelper's whole %-table. They are the
ONLY pins that can catch the port drifting from a DFU nobody re-read.

Every one resolved the checkout as a hardcoded `'../tools/parity/dfu/'`
and skipped when it was absent - which is every environment where the
reference tree lives somewhere else, including the one this project is
developed in (the clone sits outside the repo). The suite printed
`# skipped 14`, which at a glance reads exactly like `# pass 14`.

`tools/parity/prepare.sh` has honoured `DFU_PATH` since AUDIT 18 ("Point
it at a checkout you already have"); the tests simply never learned the
convention. `test/dfuRoot.mjs` is the one home now - env var first, the
in-tree sparse clone second, prepare.sh's own precedence - and with no
checkout at all the pins still skip, correctly: Port-Doctrine keeps DFU
an EXTERNAL reference, never vendored, so CI's shape is unchanged.

**All fourteen pass against the live checkout**, so the tables had not
drifted - the pins were right and blind, not wrong. Run them with:

```sh
DFU_PATH=/path/to/daggerfall-unity npm test
```

THE LESSON, and it is why this got its own slice: a skip is not a pass,
and a suite that cannot tell you which it printed is lying by omission.
The campaign taught the second half - the first version of the
env-var pin GREPPED the helper for `process.env.DFU_PATH`, and the
mutant that disabled the arm with `false ?` left the matched text
intact and survived. The pin spawns a child with the variable set and
asks where the root actually landed. **A pin that greps for a mechanism
does not test the mechanism.**

Pins: 3 in `test/parityroot.test.js` (a SOURCE SWEEP so no future test
re-hardcodes the path - the shape R6's bare-`this` sweep takes - plus
the behavioural precedence pin and the still-skips-cleanly arm).
Campaign: 5 mutants, 5 killed.

## EF1 - A COVERAGE CLAIM MUST BE MEASURED FROM BOTH SIDES (2026-08-28)

PY1's sibling, and the same failure one level up: PY1 was a pin that
never ran, this is a measurement that never asked the second question.

The effect library's `out.skipped++` had carried "the library grows one
family at a time" since the port's first magic slice, and it was picked
as the next slice on the strength of that one sentence. Three
measurements later there was no gap - and a defect the gap question
could not see.

**The first measurement used a proxy.** `effectActiveIdentity` was
asked which families it could name and answered "65 reached, 17
skipped". It is the ACTIVE-ENTRY classifier - an instant family handled
inline has no active identity by design - so Open, SpellAbsorption,
CreateItem and fourteen others were counted absent while sitting in the
file. A grep found all 17 in the port. The number was never reported as
a finding, because a number that measures the wrong thing is not a
weaker finding than the right one, it is not a finding.

**The second used the right instrument against the wrong corpus.** The
real counter, driven per key - but over a key set built by grepping
`MakeClassicKey(g, s)` for literals: 82 of DFU's 91.
`ElementalResistance.cs:194` and `PacifyEffect.cs:111` build theirs
from a loop variable, and nine real families are invisible to that
grep. Zero gaps against an incomplete corpus is not zero gaps, and the
mutation campaign now carries an arm that removes a single loop-keyed
variant (8,4) so a corpus that quietly loses them again fails.

**The third asked the other direction, and that is where the bug was.**
Sweeping all 65,536 classic keys through the real dispatcher, the port
answered 346 where DFU defines 91. The 255 extras were group 43,
subgroups 0-254: the Teleport arm tested `e.type === 43` and never its
subgroup, where DFU keys the class `MakeClassicKey(43, 255)`. Its own
comment read "(43,255)" the whole time.

THE LESSON: **"nothing is missing" and "nothing extra is answered" are
two claims, and a coverage pin that only makes the first will pass
forever on code that fails the second.** It was true on the broken
code. Whenever a pin asserts that some set is covered, ask what it says
about the things OUTSIDE the set - usually the answer is nothing, and
usually that is where the defect is.

The control arm is the other half of the discipline and costs four
lines: keys outside the classic space must REACH the counter. A
coverage pin whose measurement cannot report a miss proves nothing, and
the campaign's second mutant (delete `out.skipped++`) is exactly the
vacuous-measurement case it exists to catch.

Pins: 4 in `test/effectcoverage.test.js`. Two are UNGATED and catch the
defect in CI where no checkout exists; two REGENERATE DFU's key set
through `test/dfuRoot.mjs` (PY1's one home), so they run wherever the
tree is - and were verified against the live checkout, not left to
print a skip. Campaign: 5 mutants, 5 killed.
